intro: Before you stands the Mağlova Aqueduct, in İstanbul province, built in 1554–1563. Sinan threw this two-tier aqueduct across the Alibey stream for the Kırkçeşme water system, joining hydraulic engineering to monumental architecture in one structure.
history: Süleyman charged Sinan with bringing water to İstanbul. The hardest point of the Kırkçeşme system lay here, where the Alibey stream cuts its valley, and this is where Sinan solved it. In the great flood of 1563 the two-tier aqueduct was damaged, and he rebuilt it. Today the Alibey reservoir reaches its piers.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the two tiers of arches and the pointed cutwaters; then trace the Kırkçeşme conduit and look for the flood relief openings.
facts: Did you know? Sinan gave the piers a pointed section that splits the current, and it is this detail that has carried the structure through four and a half centuries of floods. The aqueduct was damaged in the great flood of 1563, and Sinan rebuilt it himself.
outro: This brings our tour of the Mağlova Aqueduct to an end. Please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Thank you for listening, and enjoy your visit.
